title: Pramod Bhagat, Bhavina Patel to Lead India at Asian Para Games
excerpt: The two Tokyo Paralympic medallists will carry the tricolour at the opening ceremony in Nagoya as India sends 121 athletes to the October 18–24 Games.
body:
• Pramod Bhagat and Bhavina Patel have been named India's flag bearers for the opening ceremony of the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Para Games.
  • The Games run from October 18 to 24 in Nagoya, Japan, and India is fielding a 121-member contingent — 80 men and 41 women — across six sports.
  • Bhagat won Paralympic gold in para-badminton's SL3 class at Tokyo 2020; Patel won silver in para table tennis at the same Games, India's first Paralympic table tennis medal.
  • India arrives off its best-ever Asian Para Games showing — 111 medals, including 29 gold, at Hangzhou 2022.

Two champions carry the tricolour

India's para-athletes will march into the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Para Games behind two of the country's most decorated Paralympians. Pramod Bhagat, the badminton gold medallist from Tokyo 2020, and Bhavina Patel, the table tennis silver medallist from the same Games, have been named India's flag bearers for the opening ceremony on October 18, according to the Times of India. The announcement sets the tone for a contingent that expects to build on a record-breaking campaign three years ago.

Bhagat, the shuttler from Odisha, has been the face of Indian para-badminton for nearly a decade. His gold in the men's singles SL3 category at the Tokyo Paralympics made him one of the first Indian para-shuttlers to top a Paralympic podium, and he followed it with medals at the Hangzhou Asian Para Games. Patel's Tokyo silver carried its own history: it was India's first Paralympic medal in table tennis, a breakthrough for a sport where India had never contended at that level. Both athletes have since become fixtures in India's para-sports renaissance — and now, its standard-bearers in Nagoya.

A contingent built on a record haul

This will be India's fifth appearance at the Asian Para Games, and the scale of the delegation reflects how far the movement has come. The 121 athletes will compete in six sports: archery, athletics, badminton, judo, shooting, and swimming. Athletics is the largest unit with 44 athletes, followed by badminton with 27.

The benchmark is Hangzhou 2022, where India's 309 athletes won 111 medals — 29 gold, 31 silver, and 51 bronze — the first time the country's para contingent crossed the century mark at the Games. That haul mirrored the able-bodied Asian Games performance in the same city, where India won a record 107 medals. In Nagoya, the para squad will chase both numbers and narratives: repeat appearances by stars like javelin thrower Sumit Antil and shooter Avani Lekhara, and first-time medals in newer disciplines.

What the flag-bearer choice signals

Flag-bearer selections at multi-sport events are rarely just ceremonial. Bhagat and Patel represent the two breakthrough stories of India's Paralympic movement — badminton and table tennis, sports where India went from obscurity to the podium within a single Paralympic cycle. Their selection ahead of decorated names in athletics and shooting signals the Paralympic Committee of India's confidence in the breadth of the programme, not just its depth in traditional strongholds.

The timing also matters. Para-sport in India has moved from the margins of sports coverage to the centre: para-athletes now share send-off ceremonies, government felicitations, and prime-time attention with their Olympic counterparts. A high-visibility opening-ceremony role for Bhagat and Patel extends that mainstreaming to the continental stage.

Diaspora angle

For the Indian diaspora in Japan — a community of tens of thousands concentrated in the Tokyo-Osaka corridor and growing in Nagoya's industrial belt — the Games offer a rare home-soil moment to cheer Indian athletes in person. The Aichi-Nagoya Games follow the Asian Games held in the same venues weeks earlier, where Manu Bhaker and Pawan Sehrawat carried the flag, giving Indian-origin residents a second wave of national pride.

What's next

The opening ceremony is set for October 18 at venues across Aichi prefecture, with competition running through October 24. India's preparatory camps — including the para-swimming camp at the SAI National Centre of Excellence in Gandhinagar that wrapped up October 13 — have entered their final phase. The real measure will come on the medal table: anything close to the Hangzhou century would confirm that 2022 was a foundation, not a peak.
